success_patterns: Every success answered in one step with the entity that recurs across most passages alongside the clue's anchor terms (Montgomery, France, Valentine's Day, Alice Walker, Jimmy Page). A passage sometimes held the clue near-verbatim, as in the Game Show NewsNet line for Monaco and the J! Archive and StudyStack lines for the Gadsden Purchase. Rules 2 and 3 already cover this.

Type-matching worked: a 'this ... author/guitarist' clue got a person, a 'this country' clue got a country, a 'this holiday' clue got a holiday, and a year-colon-role clue ('1968:Starring Barbra Streisand') got the film. Strategic guidance 1 and 2 already cover this.

For a 'translates to this in English' clue, the answer was the English gloss printed in parentheses right after the foreign title in the passages ('Mi Vida Loca (My Crazy Life)'). It was copied in full, not trimmed or re-translated. The skill does not describe this case.

A clue of the form 'YEAR:Starring/By <person>' asks for the work (film, album, book) from that year tied to that person. The agent picked the work that satisfied both the year and the person, and passages repeated that pairing. This is a colon-format variant that the skill only partly covers.
The head-noun test (Gadsden Purchase) and the bare common-noun test (Valentine's Day, Montgomery) both held. No change is needed to those rules.

patch.reasoning: Most successes were already covered, so only two small, low-risk additions are warranted. Both generalize across clue families and do not conflict with existing rules. (1) Translation clues: the answer is the English gloss printed beside the foreign phrase in the passages, copied in full. Without this rule, trimming or stripping rules could shorten the gloss or make the agent paraphrase it. (2) Year-prefixed colon clues ('1968:Starring X') need the type 'work from that year featuring that person'. The current colon rule covers only 'description:item' formats. Neither addition changes Rule 3 or the form rules.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Translation clues ('translates to this in English', 'means this in English', 'in English, this') ask for the English rendering of the quoted foreign word or title. Look for the gloss printed next to it in the passages (a parenthetical or 'meaning ...' after the title, e.g. 'Title (English gloss)') and copy it in full, in the passage's wording. Do not re-translate it from memory, shorten it, or answer with the foreign phrase itself.

edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content: - A year or era followed by a colon and a role ('1968:Starring Barbra Streisand', '1994:Directed by X') is a caption. It asks for the work (film, album, book, show) from that year tied to that person. Pick the title the passages pair with BOTH the year and the person, and answer with the title alone, not the person or the year.
